content:
Week 2 Objectives: Practice VPC: the network foundation for every later lab and for the workshop. Prepare the next Module 1 labs: EC2, IAM Roles for EC2, S3. Choose a lab path aligned with the fullstack developer direction. Start looking for a workshop topic for the team. Tasks to be carried out this week: Day Task Start Date Completion Date Reference Material 2 - Self-study on AWS Skill Builder, AWS Cloud Practitioner Essentials, Module 4 - Going Global: Regions, Availability Zones, edge locations and Amazon CloudFront, ways to provision AWS resources 21/09/2026 21/09/2026 https://skillbuilder.aws/learn/94T2BEN85A/aws-cloud-practitioner-essentials/ 3 - Practice lab 000003 VPC in the Singapore region (ap-southeast-1):
+ Create VPC 10.10.0.0/16 with 4 public/private subnets across 2 Availability Zones, an Internet Gateway, a Route Table for the public subnets
+ Create 3 Security Groups; enable VPC Flow Logs with an IAM role for log delivery
+ Create a key pair, launch EC2 Public and EC2 Private; SSH into EC2 Public, then SSH from it into EC2 Private (bastion)
+ Clean up all resources in the correct order
- Summarized the whole lab for review, including the parts not practiced: NAT Gateway, Reachability Analyzer, EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint, Session Manager, CloudWatch alarm
- Filtered the 127-lab catalog for the fullstack path, selected 25 labs for 12 weeks
- Learned the daily worklog rules and the program’s worklog template

https://cloudjourney.awsstudygroup.com
https://workshop-sample.awsfcaj.com/1-worklog/ 4 - Read ahead the theory and steps of lab 000048 (IAM Roles for EC2) and lab 000057 (static website on S3); noted the commands that change on Amazon Linux 2023
- Summarized and reviewed lab 000004 Compute Essentials with EC2 (9 chapters): Security Groups, EBS, snapshots, AMIs, a Node.js + MariaDB app on one instance 23/09/2026 23/09/2026 https://000048.awsstudygroup.com
https://000057.awsstudygroup.com
https://000004.awsstudygroup.com 5 - Self-study on AWS Skill Builder, AWS Cloud Practitioner Essentials, Module 5 - Networking: Amazon VPC, subnets, security groups and network ACLs, connecting to AWS, Amazon Route 53 24/09/2026 24/09/2026 https://skillbuilder.aws/learn/94T2BEN85A/aws-cloud-practitioner-essentials/ 6 - Self-study on AWS Skill Builder, AWS Cloud Practitioner Essentials, Module 6 - Storage: Amazon EBS, Amazon S3 and storage classes, Amazon EFS, block vs object vs file storage 25/09/2026 25/09/2026 https://skillbuilder.aws/learn/94T2BEN85A/aws-cloud-practitioner-essentials/ Week 2 Achievements: Built a VPC following the standard architecture: public and private subnets separated across 2 AZs, an Internet Gateway and a route table for the public subnets. Understood that the route table, not the subnet name, decides whether a subnet is public or private. Applied least privilege in Security Groups: the private instance accepts SSH only from the public instance’s Security Group, never from the Internet. Reached the private instance through a bastion; learned from the docs two safer options, EC2 Instance Connect Endpoint and Session Manager (no SSH keys, no open port 22). Enabled VPC Flow Logs to record network traffic in the VPC. Solved real issues: .pem file permissions on Windows (icacls), nested SSH not accepting “yes” (StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new). Cleaned up every resource after the lab, leaving no ongoing cost. Have a 25-lab path for the fullstack direction across the 12-week internship. Self-studied AWS Cloud Practitioner Essentials on Skill Builder, modules 4–6: core AWS service knowledge applied in labs and the project.

title: Week 6 Worklog
content:
Week 6 Objectives: Finish the v0.1.0 release: acceptance testing on staging, tagging and deploying to prod. Start Sprint 2: infrastructure for the purchase event flow, the HMAC key, the recommendations API. Tasks to be carried out this week: Day Task Start Date Completion Date Reference Material 2 - Cut release/v0.1.0 from develop (3 days later than planned; sent the team new dates: acceptance 19–21/10, tag 22/10)
- First staging deploy succeeded: shop-stg-api and shop-stg-web stacks including alarms and dashboard; 104 demo products; smoke tests read the URL from the outputs
- Created the E2E user in the staging user pool and set the staging environment variables and secret on GitHub; fixed a password mix-up caused by pasting several commands at once with a single command that generates a random password
- Re-ran the staging deploy: smoke 6/6, API E2E 4/4 files passed; sent the staging URL to the team for acceptance testing
- Reviewed and merged 3 Dependabot PRs (17 npm minor updates, 2 Python tooling updates) and Nhân’s events route contract PR into develop after the release was cut; checked the Python lockfile still matched; both dev deploys green, smoke 6/6, E2E 4/4 19/10/2026 19/10/2026 https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/how-to-create-user-accounts.html
https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_secret_set 3 - Self-study on AWS Skill Builder: started AWS Cloud Quest: Cloud Practitioner, a role-playing game course where each assignment solves a problem in a virtual city with AWS services, with hands-on labs in a real AWS environment provided by Skill Builder; follows the completed Cloud Practitioner Essentials course 20/10/2026 20/10/2026 https://aws.amazon.com/training/digital/aws-cloud-quest/ 4 - Reviewed team progress on the acceptance deadline; asked the team for results and for Sprint 2 status
- Verified 5 GitHub safeguards for Nhân’s OIDC security review issue (#180): 4 in place, found the production environment still lets admins bypass approval
- Reviewed Nhân’s synthetic dataset: ran the generator and offline evaluation, found the default catalog’s product IDs do not match the shop (0/104), re-ran with the real catalog (102/102): association rules still beat the baseline but by a smaller margin than published
- Reviewed and approved Nhân’s training data bucket PR (#179): ran tests, synthesized dev and prod through cdk-nag; the dev deploy created the bucket, smoke and E2E green
- Handled the first real alerts from staging: pre sign-up Lambda errors and p95 latency. Read the logs following the runbook: the pre sign-up Lambda was cut off at 3 seconds (128 MB gives too little CPU; cold starts ranged from 55 ms to over 3 s); the latency alarm was a false positive from cold starts under low traffic. Fixed on the release branch: pre sign-up 512 MB, 5-second timeout (PR #182); approved by Hoàng and Nhân, staging redeployed, checked the logs when Hoàng re-ran step A3: cold start down to 817 ms (previously cut off at 3,000 ms), duplicate usernames rejected correctly
- Cart acceptance testing G1–G6 on staging: guest cart kept after reload, cart merged on sign-in then on to checkout, quantities accumulate, stock limit enforced, edits and removals update the total, same cart in another browser: all passed; turned off admin bypass on the production environment
- Consolidated the team’s acceptance results: Nhân found 2 bugs (missing specs table fixed in #190, cart icon count moved to v0.2.0), Hoàng passed 5/6 account steps (enabling MFA moved to v0.2.0); ran the 4 technical checks on staging (CloudFront cache, 401, X-Ray, error logs); updated the release checklist with the results (PR #196) 21/10/2026 21/10/2026 https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-key.html
https://docs.github.com/en/actions/managing-workflow-runs-and-deployments/managing-deployments/managing-environments-for-deployment
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-memory.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-working-with-lambda-triggers.html 5 - Created the HMAC keys that anonymize userId for Nhân’s events module in all 3 environments (dev, staging, prod): SSM Parameter Store SecureString /shop/<env>/events/hmac-key, generated randomly on my machine, never committed or sent in chat; verified on dev: POST /api/v1/events returned 202 and the events table stored a hashed userIdHash with a TTL
- Released v0.1.0: opened the release/v0.1.0 → main PR (#205); CI failed at commitlint because about 10 old GitHub-generated merge commits were longer than 100 characters. Found the cause, tested the fix locally against all 100 commits, fixed it on the release branch (#207: skip merge commits ending in (#number), normal commits keep the limit); #205 went green, approved by Hoàng, merged into main
- Tagged v0.1.0; Hoàng approved the production environment deploy. The first prod deploy succeeded: shop-prd-api and shop-prd-web stacks, smoke tests 6/6, GitHub Release created automatically; edited the release notes (summary, acceptance results, what is not in this release)
- Confirmed the prod alert email; drilled the shop-prd-api-5xx alarm with set-alarm-state: received the ALARM email, then OK about 1.5 minutes later
- Merged the release branch back into develop (#209): resolved a conflict in api-stack.ts (kept Nhân’s events infrastructure and the pre sign-up fix), infra tests passed, CI green, dev redeployed
- Started Sprint 2: built the order-confirmed SNS topic and the events module’s SQS queue (PR #211): HTTPS required, SSE-SQS encryption, raw message delivery without the SNS envelope, DLQ after 5 failures kept for 14 days, queue policy accepting only this topic (threat model E9); 5 tests, dev and prod synthesized through cdk-nag. Dev deploy green; published a test message to the topic, read it back from the queue as the original JSON, then deleted it. Sent the team how to use it: Hoàng publishes from order-processor, Nhân writes the consumer that records PURCHASE
- Prepared the recommendations API: read Nhân’s nightly pipeline core (#202) and the recs table design, sent Nhân 5 questions (who creates the table, when the pipeline runs on dev, how userId is hashed, where bestsellers come from, the columns). Wrote the OpenAPI contract (PR #213): 3 routes /api/v1/recs/also-bought, for-you, bestsellers, split by access because the HTTP API JWT authorizer is attached per route; the web sends the cart’s product IDs to exclude, the server drops out-of-stock items. Checked with openapi-spec-validator; CI failed once on a flaky web test and passed on rerun; waiting for Hoàng’s review
- Rewrote the repository README in two languages for international readers (PR #215): README.md in English, README.vi.md in Vietnamese, with a language switch; added the prod demo link, a project status table and a “what this project demonstrates” section; corrected lines that described WAF and the recommendation pipeline as done. Changed the repository description to English; switched the badge to the dev deploy status (PR #217)
- Agreed with Nhân how the two halves of the recommendations fit together: the recs table format, how userId is hashed, bestsellers written ahead per category; found that the generator stops at 30/09 so the 30-day bestsellers would be empty, and that prod has no orders yet so the widgets would be empty; agreed a fallback of 30 → 90 → 365 days → newest products, and an alarm when the pipeline does not run (prod only, to stay within the 10 free alarms)
- Built the recs table (PR #221): pk/sk keys, TTL, on-demand, exposed so Nhân’s pipeline can grant itself write access; 5 tests, checked the table on dev
- Wrote the recommendations API core (PR #224): selection rules (keep the pipeline’s rank, drop out-of-stock, inactive and in-cart products) and 3 use cases for frequently bought together, for you and bestsellers, with fallbacks when data is missing; 12 tests, layer rules checked 22/10/2026 22/10/2026 https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html
https://commitlint.js.org/reference/configuration.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/cloudwatch/set-alarm-state.html
https://git-scm.com/docs/git-merge#_how_to_resolve_conflicts
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-sqs-as-subscriber.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sns/latest/dg/sns-large-payload-raw-message-delivery.html 6 - Self-study on AWS Skill Builder: continued AWS Cloud Quest: Cloud Practitioner, building solutions in the real AWS environment provided by Skill Builder 23/10/2026 23/10/2026 https://aws.amazon.com/training/digital/aws-cloud-quest/ 7 - Answered Hoàng’s ordering design questions and settled the approach: cross-module table access goes into one ADR-0017 revision written by Hoàng (ordering reads products and carts and writes only the stock column; the recommendations API reads products; the recommendations pipeline may Scan products read-only); removed the admin email from the order-confirmed topic; new alarms only in prod to stay within the 10 free alarms; if sending to SQS fails after the order is written, still return 201 and log plus emit a metric
- Reviewed the ordering PRs Hoàng had merged (#233, #234, #236, #237): they match the decisions; reminded the team to wait for one approval before merging infrastructure and contract PRs
- Checked that Nhân’s shared userId hash PR (#225) is in develop, so the recommendations API hashes the same way as the events module 24/10/2026 24/10/2026 https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/specifying-conditions.html CN - Finished the recommendations API (PR #241): adapters for the recs table (version pointer kept 60 seconds in the Lambda, Query up to 20 rows) and the products table (BatchGetItem with retries for unprocessed keys); handler validating limit 1–10, exclude up to 20 IDs and category; Lambda and 3 routes: also-bought and bestsellers public, for-you requires sign-in; IAM reads only the right tables and the HMAC key. Added a NEWEST source to the contract for when the shop has too few orders to rank bestsellers
- Verified locally: unit tests, integration tests against DynamoDB Local in Docker, cdk synth with cdk-nag, layer rules; CI green, approved by Hoàng
- Found the API read a different product ID column than agreed with Nhân; the PR was merged before the fix landed, so opened a separate fix PR (#246) and asked Nhân to rename the column in the pipeline and write 20 rows per product
- Dev deploy green; called the 3 routes on dev: empty list while the pipeline has not run, 400 for bad parameters, 401 for for-you without sign-in
- Settled 3 points with Hoàng for the order confirmation worker: read the customer email with Cognito ListUsers filtered by sub, only the email attribute, never stored or logged; create the SES sender identity once with the CLI instead of CDK because dev, staging and prod share one account and region; keep SES in the sandbox in all 3 environments (200 emails/day, 1 email/second) and asked Hoàng to handle throttling. Verified the sender address and stored it as a repository secret; updated deploy.yml and deploy-prod.yml to pass the sender to CDK the same way as the alarm email, and renamed the E2E step per ADR-0018 (PR #261); dev deploy green, address masked in logs
- Reviewed Hoàng’s ordering PRs that were merged before review (#248 order handler and OrderEnqueueFailed alarm, #254 removing the IAM condition that blocked stock updates): fine; noted the account now has 12 alarms, about 0.2 USD/month over the free tier as the team accepted; checked that Nhân’s recs format PR (#250) matches the recommendations API 25/10/2026 25/10/2026 https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/Query.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/APIReference/API_BatchGetItem.html
https://node.testcontainers.org/

title: Week 7 Worklog
content:
Week 7 Objectives: Prepare the v0.2.0 release: cut the release branch on 30/10, tag on 02/11. Get product recommendations working on dev: Nhân’s nightly pipeline writes the recs table, the recommendations API returns data, widgets on the web. Finish and publish Blog 1. Tasks to be carried out this week: Day Task Start Date Completion Date Reference Material 2 - Reviewed the PRs the team merged over the weekend without review: order confirmation worker infrastructure (#263), worker SES emails (#265), order E2E fix (#267), Nhân’s nightly recommendations job (#269). The worker has narrow IAM permissions, only the worker may publish to the order-confirmed topic, and concurrency is capped at 2 to fit the SES sandbox limit of 1 email/second; the email code follows the agreed decisions but is not enabled yet, pending the SES and Cognito permissions PR. Found why the #265 deploy failed (E2E expected a PENDING order while the worker had already confirmed it), fixed by #267
- Reviewed and merged 4 Dependabot PRs (17 npm packages including AWS SDK, CDK, vite; ruff; uv-build; the setup-uv action); final dev deploy green, verified uv.lock and pnpm-lock.yaml still match
- Prepared Blog 1 on deploying with OIDC: checked every technical detail against the github-oidc.yaml template, the workflow, PR #25, the timed run, GitHub Environments rules and GitHub’s docs on immutable subjects; updated the numbers (118 successful deploys on develop); corrected the incident section to what I remember and can verify; the illustration was made with AI tool assistance, disclosed in the post. Not published yet
- Closed the OIDC review (#180) by accepting the risk: re-checked the 5 GitHub safeguards (environments accept only the right branch/tag, production needs 1 of 3 reviewers, self-review blocked, admins cannot bypass, only admins create v* tags); fixed ADR-0013 to state that deploy roles still use cfn-exec-role with AdministratorAccess, updated threat model C6 and E9 (PR #278, awaiting review)
- Fixed 2 alarms that fired falsely on staging on 21/10 (PR #280, awaiting review): api-latency-p95 uses metric math to count only periods with at least 20 requests; presignup-errors subtracts sign-up rejections counted by a metric filter on the Lambda logs, while still alerting on real errors such as timeouts
- Drafted the v0.2.0 acceptance checklist (PR #282) based on the v0.1.0 one: reviewed sprint 2 scope, test tables for ordering, recommendations and security assigned to someone other than the author; found 4 gaps (SES email not enabled, web not sending events and no recommendation widget, no cancel order button, admin and WAF not started) and asked the team to decide before 30/10
- The team settled v0.2.0 scope: admin and WAF move to v1.0.0-rc.1, I build the recommendation widget; updated the checklist (PR #286). Corrected my wrong claim about the cancel order button (it already exists on the web)
- Reviewed 2 PRs Hoàng merged without approval: worker infrastructure (#263) and email permissions (#284). Checked the SES docs on IAM in the sandbox and accepted ses:SendEmail on identity/* with an ses:FromAddress condition
- Verified the worker on dev with the AWS CLI: all environment variables present, logs only show not_verified warnings for E2E orders (no AccessDenied, no email addresses), orders queue and DLQ empty 26/10/2026 26/10/2026 https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/control-user-access.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/STS/latest/APIReference/API_AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-scaling.html 3 - Checked the first real run of the nightly recommendations job on dev (asked by Nhân): the 02:00 schedule ran once, 0 errors, 4 seconds; no AccessDeniedException; the ACTIVE# pointers of all 3 recommendation types moved to the new version, bestsellers based on PURCHASES_30D; called the API on dev: bestsellers and “frequently bought together” returned sensible results. Asked Nhân whether prod mixes synthetic events and about logs not yet in JSON
- Homepage recommendation widget (PR #289): guests see “Đang được mua nhiều”, signed-in users see “Dành cho bạn”; the block hides on error or empty results; it waits for the sign-in status before calling the API so the title does not flicker; 5 new tests, tried against the dev API through the Vite proxy; merged and deployed to dev
- “Thường mua kèm” widget at the bottom of the product page (PR #292): excludes items already in the cart with the exclude parameter and refetches when the cart changes; hides the block when there are no recommendations; added Nhân’s note on synthetic data to the v0.2.0 release notes
- Verified the homepage widget on dev after signing in, using the API Gateway access logs: /recs/for-you returned 200 (266–414 ms), and an account with no history got bestsellers as designed; the widget passes on dev. Noted that /recs/bestsellers takes about 1.5 seconds on a Lambda cold start, to optimize after v0.2.0
- Reviewed and approved Nhân’s PR #294 (the recommendations job now prints a single JSON line for Logs Insights); suggested adding the data check counts to the summary line
- Approved the plan for an OWASP ZAP baseline scan (passive only) of the dev site for threat model C3 and L4: dev only, no AJAX spider, not during a deploy or on the release cut day
- Checked Blog 1 before publishing: the sentence is fixed, the post and diagram do not expose the account ID; screenshots still need the account ID masked
- Read Nhân’s ZAP baseline results (0 FAIL, 12 WARN, 56 PASS) and checked the dev site headers myself: the “Server leaks version” warning is only Server: AmazonS3; the SRI warning comes from the Google Fonts link; COEP should not be enabled because it would block the fonts. Created issue #299 for a CloudFront response headers policy (L4) after v0.2.0, noting that the CSP must allow Cognito and Google Fonts
- Reviewed, approved and merged Nhân’s PR #301: threat model L4 now rates the ZAP warnings correctly, with SRI and COEP accepted with reasons
- Fixed a bug Hoàng found while reviewing #289 (PR #303): signing out did not clear the recommendations cache, so the next person signing in on the same device briefly saw the previous user’s “Dành cho bạn”; signing out now clears the recs cache, with a test that fails before the fix; approved by Hoàng and deployed to dev 27/10/2026 27/10/2026 https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/dependent-queries

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/scheduler/latest/UserGuide/what-is-scheduler.html 4 - Worked at the office with Hoàng
- Reviewed v0.2.0 progress and ran section 1 of the checklist early: dev deploy green, no open security alerts (Dependabot, CodeQL, secret scanning all 0), October cost by env tag close to zero
- O7 acceptance on dev: read the worker logs and SES sending statistics (5 emails sent, 0 bounces), and Hoàng confirmed receiving both the confirmation and cancellation emails
- Split security work with Nhân: Nhân owns WAF end to end, I own C1 (blocking direct execute-api calls); flagged WAF cost while not on the CloudFront Free plan and that the WebACL must live in us-east-1
- Went through a reviewed bug list: the pre sign-up Lambda could call ListUsers on every user pool, including prod since all environments share one account. Checked the Service Authorization Reference (the userpool resource supports aws:ResourceTag), added an env tag condition, verified the tag on all 4 real user pools, wrote a failing test before the fix; CI green, awaiting Nhân’s review 28/10/2026 28/10/2026 https://docs.aws.amazon.com/service-authorization/latest/reference/list_cognito-idp.html

Checked after the dev deploy: signing up with a new username works; invoking the Lambda directly with a test event rejects a duplicate username (USERNAME_TAKEN); the IAM Policy Simulator on the real role allows the dev pool and denies the staging and prod pools. This also confirmed that the #280 metric filter counts the rejection and the alarm does not fire falsely
- Checked Nhân’s WAF proposal against the CloudFront flat-rate pricing plans docs: accounts on the AWS Free Tier cannot subscribe to a plan, so the free WAF approach of ADR-0006 is not possible. Decided on pay-as-you-go WAF on prod only (about $10/month, paid from credits); Nhân will update ADR-0006 in the WAF PR
